title: Nvidia falls under SEC accounting probe as shares drop roughly 14%
subtitle: Reuters and the Wall Street Journal say the SEC is examining whether Nvidia's disclosures around a concentration of Singapore revenue and AI financing deals misled investors.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Reuters reported on Thursday evening — followed by the Wall Street Journal — that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is examining Nvidia's accounting practices, citing people briefed on the matter. The probe reportedly covers whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, with particular attention to roughly $104 billion in revenue booked through the company's Singapore unit in 2025 — about half of its sales for the year. Nvidia delayed its 10-Q quarterly filing to 'the coming weeks' and disclosed an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee. Shares fell nearly 14% on Friday, the worst single-day drop since the DeepSeek-triggered rout in January 2025.

An SEC inquiry is not evidence of wrongdoing — the agency can open and close an exam without any finding. But the matter arrives at a bad moment. Analysts have spent weeks worrying out loud about circular financing in the AI build-out, where chip vendors, cloud providers and model labs cross-invest in one another's capacity. On Nvidia's Tuesday call, interim CEO Colette Kress said the company would be 'far more selective' about AI industry financing deals going forward — a notable shift in tone from the backstop-heavy posture of the Jensen Huang era.

The pressure is compounding. Washington's Commerce Department has a pending rule to block Chinese firms from remotely accessing U.S. AI chips, and Nvidia has stopped shipping its Hopper-generation parts to China even where sales were approved. The Justice Department is still reviewing the $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal. Anthropic used its IPO roadshow to brag that its Claude Mythos model ported a workload to AMD chips in three days. Any single item is manageable; together they chip at the assumption that Nvidia's margins and growth are an immovable law of the AI economy.

A note for learners: 'accounting investigation' is doing a lot of work in that headline. What actually matters is whether Nvidia's reported revenue reflects goods and services it will ultimately keep, or whether some portion is booked against financing arrangements it funded itself. Follow the 10-Q when it drops — the geographic breakdown and the related-party disclosures are where the story lives. Price action without a filing is noise.
